headline_marked: [[Illegal liquor seized]] from Fu-Wang and three other Dhaka establishments in NBR raids
headline: Illegal liquor seized from Fu-Wang and three other Dhaka establishments in NBR raids
summary: Joint raids by four NBR intelligence agencies seized 230 bottles of "illegal" liquor from Fu-Wang Bowling and Services, owned by Salman Muqtadir's father-in-law. Similar raids also targeted three other establishments in Dhaka, uncovering more unapproved liquor
details: Joint raids by four National Board of Revenue (NBR) intelligence agencies seized 230 bottles of "illegal" liquor from Fu-Wang Bowling and Services in Gulshan. The establishment is owned by Sheikh Nur Islam, father-in-law of content creator Salman Muqtadir.

The raid on Fu-Wang occurred as bottles were being moved in a covered van, which was subsequently detained along with the stock. Officials also seized packets of "ginseng" and 1kg of "saffron" for which no valid import or purchase papers could be provided.

Besides Fu-Wang, the NBR teams raided Raw Canvas Restaurant, Holiday Inn (operating as Habib Hotel International), and Margherita Lounge. This operation is part of a broader NBR campaign against revenue evasion and illegal stockpiling.

At Margherita Lounge in Uttara, officials discovered 608 litres of liquor, with only 36 litres being locally produced. The establishment lacked valid approval for the foreign liquor and presented questionable purchase documents for the local stock.

The Holiday Inn International hotel in Tejgaon, managed by InterContinental Hotels Group (IHG), also faced a raid where its bar was found to lack a license in the hotel's name. Officials stated that approval from the Department of Narcotics Control was required but not presented.

Raw Canvas Bar and Restaurant in Gulshan saw the seizure of 29 litres of "unapproved" liquor. Separately, a bonded warehouse, Toss Bond Private Limited, was raided for allegedly stocking duty-free liquor in "unauthorised" godowns.

NBR officials identified Nur Islam as the owner of the warehouse, though Fu-Wang denies any link. The tax intelligence agencies have been investigating alleged irregularities in the liquor and bar business, as well as Nur's family's Canadian citizenship and assets.

CIID officials emphasized that raids are based on intelligence and records, not individuals or groups, dismissing any perceived coincidence. The probe intensified after Salman Muqtadir publicly blamed those in power for an attack on his studio.

headline_marked: [[Shai Hope's unbeaten 162]] leads West Indies to five-wicket victory over India, denying series sweep
headline: Shai Hope's unbeaten 162 leads West Indies to five-wicket victory over India, denying series sweep
summary: Shai Hope's magnificent 162* off 143 balls anchored the chase, securing a five-wicket win for West Indies in the final ODI and preventing India from a clean sweep.
details: Shai Hope anchored the chase with an unbeaten 162 off 143 balls as West Indies prevented India from completing a series sweep with a five-wicket victory in the third and final one-day international in New Chandigarh.
After the early loss of John Campbell in the fifth over, Hope combined with Amir Jangoo for a crucial 109-run stand to steady the innings, helping West Indies reach 78-1 at the end of the powerplay.

Jangoo struck his third ODI half-century before being run out for 67, while Sherfane Rutherford fell soon after for 24. Hope, however, maintained the momentum, adding another vital 56-run partnership to keep the chase on track.

Despite the dismissals of Keemo Paul and Matthew Forde, Hope remained in control of the chase. Gudakesh Motie contributed a brisk 19 off 14 balls, as West Indies sealed victory with 10 balls to spare.

Earlier, India were forced to rebuild after slipping to 4-2, but Rohit Sharma and Ruturaj Gaikwad steadied the innings with a 137-run partnership. Sharma anchored the recovery with a fluent 92 off 85 balls before falling eight runs short of a century.

After Rohit's dismissal, KL Rahul made the most of his lone batting opportunity of the series, bringing up his ninth ODI hundred. Rahul accelerated sharply at the death, smashing 42 runs off the final 12 balls he faced to convert his century into a career-best ODI score.

With Rahul unbeaten on 129, India finished strongly through late cameos from Naman Dhir (30 off 21 balls) and Anshul Kamboj (17 off nine balls). Their contributions helped propel India to 351-7, with Rahul and Gurnoor Brar unbeaten at the crease.
The Shubman Gill-led side had already secured the series by winning the opening two ODIs. In the second match, India completed a record chase of 406 with 6.3 overs to spare to seal the series.
